identifiers.title: The effect of turmeric and black pepper powder incorporated in breakfast on postprandial glycemia, appetite, palatability, and gastrointestinal well-being in normal-weight adults
identifiers.authors: Khan S, Arif M, Laraib H, Naqvi SN, Shah OA, Farooq U, Sami-Ullah M, Khan GA
identifiers.citation: Khan S, Arif M, Laraib H, et al. The effect of turmeric and black pepper powder incorporated in breakfast on postprandial glycemia, appetite, palatability, and gastrointestinal well-being in normal-weight adults. Food Sci Nutr. 2024;12(4):2846-2854.

facts.label: Design: randomized crossover, four test meals, each with 50 g of carbohydrate

facts.quote: Every subject attended four sessions with 1 week washout period between the trials.

facts.label: Overnight fast before each visit
facts.value: they were asked to fast
facts.quote: Selected personnel were instructed to take their twilight meal up to 10:00 p.m. following which they were asked to fast

facts.label: The four test meals and the spice doses
facts.value: +1 g black pepper (BP)
facts.quote: Test foods were: (1) bread toast and egg (control diet), (2) bread toast and egg +1 g black pepper (BP), (3) bread toast and egg +1 g turmeric (TR), and (4) bread toast and egg +1 g black pepper +1 g turmeric (BP + TR), all meals were served with tea.

facts.label: How the spice was given: powder mixed into the fried egg
facts.value: were added to the egg
facts.quote: In test meals black pepper (1 g) and turmeric powder (1 g) were added to the egg.

facts.label: What else was on the plate: two toasts and a cup of sweet milk tea
facts.value: 2 standard bread toasts
facts.quote: The fried egg was served with 2 standard bread toasts and a cup of black tea (250 mL) having 200 mL milk, 50 mL water, 1 teaspoon black tea (5 g), and 1 tablespoon sugar (8 g).

facts.label: Meal eaten within 10 minutes
facts.value: were ingested in 10 min
facts.quote: Next, the test meals, supplying 50 g of accessible carbohydrates, were ingested in 10 min.

facts.label: When blood glucose was measured

facts.quote: blood glucose levels were recorded at 0, 30, 60, 120, and 180 min

facts.quote: was employed to compute the blood glucose, and samples were collected via finger prick

facts.label: differed from the control meal 30 minutes after eating, for the pepper meal and the pepper-plus-turmeric meal (p = .023); the text gives no size for the difference
facts.value: show a significant effect for blood glucose level at the time point 30 min
facts.quote: So test meals (BP and BP + TR) show a significant effect for blood glucose level at the time point 30 min as compared to reference meal (C) (p = .023).

facts.label: lower than the control meal after the pepper meal and the pepper-plus-turmeric meal (p < .05); direction stated in the abstract, no size given
facts.value: resulted in lower blood glycemia
facts.quote: Experimental meals BP and BP + TR resulted in lower blood glycemia (p < .05) significantly compared to control meal.

facts.label: no significant difference between the four meals over the whole 3 hours
facts.value: shows a non-significant effect
facts.quote: Incremental area under the curves (iAUCs) among the test meals shows a non‐significant effect.

facts.label: turmeric alone: no effect on blood glucose compared with the control meal
facts.value: no remarkable effect of TR (1 g) meal on postprandial blood sugar level was noticed
facts.quote: Contradictory to the assumption of this current approach, no remarkable effect of TR (1 g) meal on postprandial blood sugar level was noticed.
facts.outcome: Blood glucose after the turmeric-only meal

facts.label: Authors' guess at why turmeric alone did nothing: the dose was low
facts.value: the use of low dose of turmeric powder
facts.quote: A possible rationale for this may be the use of low dose of turmeric powder in this study.

facts.label: less hunger and less perceived eating ability, more satiety, after the pepper meal and the pepper-plus-turmeric meal; no sizes given
facts.value: A decrease in perceived eating ability and hunger, and an increase in satiety after BP + TR and BP meal was observed
facts.quote: A decrease in perceived eating ability and hunger, and an increase in satiety after BP + TR and BP meal was observed.
facts.outcome: Self-rated hunger, satiety and how much they felt they could eat

facts.label: no significant difference between meals
facts.value: the effect of treatment on fullness is not statistically significant
facts.quote: However, in our study, the effect of treatment on fullness is not statistically significant but both of these meals (BP and BP + TR) have increased fullness as compared to TR and control meal.

facts.label: Appetite was rated by the participants on 100 mm lines
facts.value: Appetite was assessed by using VAS
facts.quote: Appetite was assessed by using VAS (Flint et al., ). The VAS consisted of four scales, each of 100 mm length, which was used to determine the participant's hunger from 0 to 100 mm

facts.label: no significant difference between meals or over time (p > .05)
facts.value: There was no significant (p > .05) effect of time, treatment, and time × treatment on postprandial responses of gastrointestinal symptoms
facts.quote: There was no significant (p > .05) effect of time, treatment, and time × treatment on postprandial responses of gastrointestinal symptoms.

facts.label: Gut symptoms were rated by the participants on a 4-point scale
facts.value: assessed using a 4‐point Likert scale
facts.quote: Gastrointestinal symptoms such as swelling of stomach, uneasy feelings, flatulence, loose stools, diarrhea, constipation, cramping, and grumbling were assessed using a 4‐point Likert scale.

facts.label: Taste was rated on a 9-point scale from dislike extremely to like extremely
facts.value: A 9‐point hedonic calibration
facts.quote: A 9‐point hedonic calibration was exploited with dislike extremely on one end and like extremely on the other end.

facts.label: the control meal and the combined meal were rated higher than the pepper-only and turmeric-only meals (p < .05)
facts.value: the control meal and combined meal have significantly (p < .05) higher acceptability than (BP and TR) meal
facts.quote: Post hoc pair‐wise comparison shows that the control meal and combined meal have significantly (p < .05) higher acceptability than (BP and TR) meal in comparison of general appearance, consistency, smell, taste, and whole pleasantness.
facts.outcome: Palatability (appearance, texture, smell, taste, overall pleasantness)

facts.label: Black pepper's main active ingredient is piperine
facts.value: with the main active ingredient piperine
facts.quote: Black pepper (Piper nigrum) family piperaceae, with the main active ingredient piperine, has a hypoglycaemic effect (Panda & Kar, ).

facts.label: Authors' proposed mechanism: pepper compounds might act on the TRPV1 receptor
facts.value: which might act on receptor TRPV1
facts.quote: It was found that these effects are owing to the bio‐active profile of black pepper, such as isopiperine, isochavicine, piperine, piperanine, piperolein A and B, which might act on receptor TRPV1

facts.label: TRPV1 is in the mouth; the authors say its activation is known to affect glucose control and appetite
facts.value: TRPV1 is present in the oral cavity
facts.quote: TRPV1 is present in the oral cavity and its activation is widely known to improve glucose homeostasis, potentially affect appetite responses as well as increase energy metabolism.

facts.label: TRPV1 activation raises GLP-1 in the lower small intestine and the blood (earlier work the authors cite)
facts.value: TRPV1 activation increases GLP‐1
facts.quote: Furthermore, TRPV1 activation increases GLP‐1; glucagon‐like peptide‐1 levels in the ileum and plasma.

facts.label: Earlier work on the two spices together was in animals only
facts.value: conducted only on animals not on humans
facts.quote: Previously such types of investigations were conducted only on animals not on humans.

facts.label: The authors call this an acute intervention (one meal per condition)
facts.value: in this acute intervention
facts.quote: The decrease in hunger and perceived eating ability and increase in satiety and fullness after BP + TR and BP meal in this acute intervention

facts.label: The authors' own stated limitation: the glycemic index of the meals was not measured
facts.value: The glycemic index of the test meals was not noted
facts.quote: This study has some deficiencies. The glycemic index of the test meals was not noted and it necessitates the need to be explored in future research studies.

facts.label: The proposed mechanism was not measured: no hormones were examined
facts.value: hormones involved in the regulation of satiety were not examined
facts.quote: However, hormones involved in the regulation of satiety were not examined in this intervention.

facts.label: The drop in hunger may be a taste effect: the spiced meals were liked less
facts.value: might be because of decreased palatability
facts.quote: The reported reduction in hunger after BP and BP + TR meal consumption might be because of decreased palatability since different scientific approaches have revealed an enormous effect of palatability on appetite

facts.label: The authors say the mechanisms still need investigating
facts.value: actual physiological mechanisms involved in these effects need further investigation
facts.quote: The potential components of turmeric and black pepper and actual physiological mechanisms involved in these effects need further investigation.

facts.label: No long-term data: the authors call for long-term studies
facts.value: Future long‐term studies
facts.quote: Future long‐term studies with increased dosage of turmeric and black pepper are considered necessary to understand the advantages of long‐term utilization of turmeric and black pepper supplemented breakfast
